title: Nonpositive finite free tensor preserves pseudo-coherence after a closed pushforward
statement:
Let $j:P\hookrightarrow W$ be a closed immersion of affine schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $m\in\mathbf Z$ and $Q\in D(\mathcal O_P)$ [def-pc-derived-category]. Let $F^\bullet$ be a cochain complex of $\mathcal O_P$-modules with $F^q=0$ for $q>0$ and $F^q\cong\mathcal O_P^{\oplus r_q}$ for a finite nonnegative integer $r_q$ for each $q\leq0$; $F^\bullet$ also denotes its image in the derived category. Suppose $Rj_*Q$ [def-pc-derived-direct-image] is $m$-pseudo-coherent on $W$ [def-sfb-m-pseudo-coherent-complex]. Then
$$Rj_*(Q\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_P}F^\bullet)$$
is $m$-pseudo-coherent on $W$, using the derived tensor of [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure]. There is no quasi-coherence or lower cohomological bound assumption on $Q$, and $F^\bullet$ need not be bounded below.

source.place: Tag 09US, lemma-pull-relative-pseudo-coherent, tensor-filtration paragraph, extracted as an absolute closed-pushforward lemma; replace the printed tail inequality by vanishing in degrees greater than or equal to the cutoff.

proof.text: Put $A=Rj_*Q$. Work locally on $W$: for an open $U\subset W$ put $V=j^{-1}U$ and $j_U:V\hookrightarrow U$. This is still a closed immersion: its image is the intersection of the closed image of $j$ with $U$, and its local-ring maps are the same surjections. The exact closed-pushforward statement computes both $Rj_*$ and $Rj_{U*}$ termwise. The ordinary pushforward/open-restriction comparison, applied termwise, identifies $A|_U$ with $Rj_{U*}(Q|_V)$. Open restriction is exact and hence preserves quasi-isomorphisms; it preserves K-flatness and commutes with total tensor. Applying these last two facts to a K-flat tensor representative identifies the restriction of our target with $Rj_{U*}(Q|_V\otimes^{\mathbf L}F|_V)$. Thus it suffices to prove the assertion on an open cover of $W$.

source.place: Tag 09US, lemma-pull-relative-pseudo-coherent, tensor-filtration paragraph; cutoff and finite induction made explicit.

proof.text: Choose the cover in the definition of $m$-pseudo-coherence for $A$, and fix one member $U$ with a strictly perfect approximation $B\to A|_U$. Choose $a\ge m$ above all nonzero degrees of $B$. Then $H^i(A|_U)=0$ for $i>a$, since $i>m$ and the approximation is an isomorphism in that range. Exactness of $j_{U*}$ and exact-functor cohomology give $j_{U*}H^i(Q|_V)=0$ for $i>a$. Closed pushforward detects zero sheaves: each open of $V$ has the form $j_U^{-1}T$ for an open $T\subset U$, and $(j_{U*}G)(T)=G(j_U^{-1}T)$, so $j_{U*}G=0$ implies $G=0$. Therefore $H^i(Q|_V)=0$ for $i>a$. From now on suppress $U,V$ in the notation. No global upper bound or quasi-coherence has been used.

source.place: Tag 09US, lemma-pull-relative-pseudo-coherent, tensor-filtration paragraph; cutoff and finite induction made explicit.

proof.text: Choose a cochain representative $E_0$ of the restricted $Q$ and replace it by $E=\tau_{\le a}E_0$. Explicitly $E^p=E_0^p$ for $p<a$, $E^a=\ker d_{E_0}^a$, and $E^p=0$ for $p>a$. The inclusion into $E_0$ preserves cohomology in degrees $\le a$ and both sides have zero cohomology above $a$, so it is a quasi-isomorphism. Every finite free sheaf is flat: tensoring with $\mathcal O^{\oplus r}$ is the finite direct-sum functor, which preserves kernels and cokernels coordinatewise. Consequently $F$, bounded above by zero with finite free terms, is K-flat. The derived-tensor definition and exact closed pushforward now identify the local target with the image of $C=j_*\operatorname{Tot}(E\otimes F)$. Its degree-$n$ sum has only finitely many possibly nonzero summands: $p+q=n$, $p\le a$, $q\le0$ imply $n-a\le q\le0$.

source.place: Tag 09US, lemma-pull-relative-pseudo-coherent, tensor-filtration paragraph; cutoff and finite induction made explicit.

proof.text: For every $q\le0$ and finite $r$, $A^{\oplus r}[-q]$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent. Indeed, on each approximation open take the finite sum of its strictly perfect witness and shift it by $-q$. Such a complex is still bounded with finite-free-retract terms. Its map to $A^{\oplus r}[-q]$ has cohomology the finite sum of the original map in degree $i-q$: if $i>m$ then $i-q>m$, and if $i=m$ then $m-q\ge m$, giving an isomorphism or a surjection as required. Here $H^i(A[-q])=H^{i-q}(A)$ by the cochain shift convention. For $r=0$ use the zero complex. This proves the assertion directly from the approximation definition, rather than assuming all-degree pseudo-coherence.

source.place: Tag 09US, lemma-pull-relative-pseudo-coherent, tensor-filtration paragraph; cutoff and finite induction made explicit.

proof.text: For $c\le0$ put $F_c=\sigma_{\ge c}F$ and $C_c=j_*\operatorname{Tot}(E\otimes F_c)$, and put $F_1=C_1=0$. The sequence $0\to F_{c+1}\to F_c\to F^c[-c]\to0$ is split in every degree, with the quotient concentrated in degree $c$. Tensor totalization has, degreewise, the corresponding direct-sum decomposition; after the additive functor $j_*$ it remains a degreewise split short exact sequence. Its quotient is isomorphic to $(j_*E)^{\oplus r_c}[-c]$: use a basis of $F^c\cong\mathcal O^{\oplus r_c}$ and in total degree $n$ multiply by $(-1)^{cn}$ to match the shifted differential $(-1)^c d_E$. All sums in a fixed degree are finite by the preceding bounds, so no assertion about infinite sums under $j_*$ is needed. The degreewise-split triangle lemma gives the distinguished triangle $C_{c+1}\to C_c\to A^{\oplus r_c}[-c]\to C_{c+1}[1]$.

source.place: Tag 09US, lemma-pull-relative-pseudo-coherent, tensor-filtration paragraph; cutoff and finite induction made explicit.

proof.text: Fix any $c\le0$. Descending finite induction from $C_1=0$ proves that $C_c$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent. The zero witness proves the base. At the step from $t+1$ to $t$, the first vertex $C_{t+1}$ has the induction property and the third vertex $A^{\oplus r_t}[-t]$ has it by step 4, since $t\le0$. Apply clause (2) of the ringed-site $m$-pseudo-coherent triangle lemma to the triangle of step 5 to obtain it for the middle vertex $C_t$. On the Zariski site its approximation notion is exactly our scheme notion: an open cover of the space restricts to covers of every open, and conversely one applies the site definition to the whole space. This is a finite induction to the chosen $c$, with no claim about closure under infinite filtrations.

source.place: Tag 09US, lemma-pull-relative-pseudo-coherent, tensor-filtration paragraph; cutoff and finite induction made explicit.

proof.text: Take $c=\min(0,m-a)$, so $a+c\le m$. Put $L=F/F_c$, whose terms vanish for $q\ge c$. The quotient $D=C/C_c$ is $j_*\operatorname{Tot}(E\otimes L)$, because the inclusion splits in each total degree. A nonzero summand in degree $n$ requires $p\le a$ and $q\le c-1$, hence $n=p+q\le a+c-1\le m-1$. Thus $D^n=0$ for every $n\ge m$, and in particular $H^n(D)=0$ there. The map from the zero strictly perfect complex to $D$ is an isomorphism on cohomology above $m$ and a surjection at $m$, so $D$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent. This is the required direction of the tail bound; no lower bound on either complex is asserted.

source.place: Tag 09US, lemma-pull-relative-pseudo-coherent, tensor-filtration paragraph; cutoff and finite induction made explicit.

proof.text: The degreewise split exact sequence $0\to C_c\to C\to D\to0$ gives a distinguished triangle by the same split-triangle lemma (the degreewise retraction and section are projection and inclusion of the retained and discarded column summands). Both end vertices are $m$-pseudo-coherent by steps 6 and 7. Clause (2) of the ringed-site triangle lemma therefore proves that $C$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent on $U$. Step 3 identifies $C$ with the local target. Repeating for the approximation cover chosen in step 2, the restriction comparison in step 1 and the open-cover definition give the stated conclusion on $W$.
